summary: Wilde, in Rome in April 1900, took up Arnaldo - Armando's greatest friend - the same week he gave Armando up: 'I now like Arnaldo: he was Armando's greatest friend, but the friendship is over.' The whole of the record for Arnaldo.
certainty_reasoning: One sentence, in the same letter where Wilde gives up Armando and takes up his best friend; the armando--wilde record already reads the exchange as Wilde moving his interest to Arnaldo. The declaration is Wilde's own; outcome unknown.

sources.quote: I now like Arnaldo: he was Armando's greatest friend, but the friendship is over.
sources.context: Wilde to Robert Ross, Rome, April 1900, in the sentence immediately after giving up Armando. The whole of the record for Arnaldo.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: That Wilde replaced one young Roman with his best friend, and said so plainly.
